nodes.title: Administrative Procedure Act
nodes.summary: The foundational statute governing federal agency rulemaking and adjudication. Establishes requirements for notice-and-comment rulemaking, formal rulemaking, and judicial review of agency actions.
nodes.text: The Administrative Procedure Act (APA) governs the process by which federal agencies develop and issue regulations. It includes requirements for publishing notices of proposed rulemaking in the Federal Register, giving interested persons an opportunity to participate through submission of written comments, and publishing a general statement of basis and purpose when final rules are issued.

nodes.title: Freedom of Information Act
nodes.summary: Provides public access to federal agency records. Establishes nine exemptions and requires agencies to proactively disclose certain information.
nodes.text: The Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) provides that any person has a right to obtain access to federal agency records, except to the extent that such records are protected from public disclosure by one of nine exemptions or by one of three special law enforcement record exclusions.

nodes.title: Privacy Act of 1974
nodes.summary: Governs the collection, maintenance, use, and dissemination of personally identifiable information maintained by federal agencies.
nodes.text: The Privacy Act of 1974 establishes a code of fair information practices that governs the collection, maintenance, use, and dissemination of information about individuals that is maintained in systems of records by federal agencies.

nodes.title: Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act
nodes.summary: Protects the privacy of student education records and gives parents rights to access and amend their children's records.
nodes.text: FERPA gives parents certain rights with respect to their children's education records. These rights transfer to the student when he or she reaches the age of 18 or attends a school beyond the high school level.

nodes.title: Clean Air Act
nodes.summary: Comprehensive federal law regulating air emissions from stationary and mobile sources. Authorizes EPA to establish National Ambient Air Quality Standards.
nodes.text: The Clean Air Act is the comprehensive federal law that regulates air emissions from stationary and mobile sources. This law authorizes the EPA to establish National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) to protect public health and welfare.

nodes.title: National Environmental Policy Act
nodes.summary: Requires federal agencies to assess environmental effects of proposed actions before making decisions.
nodes.text: NEPA requires federal agencies to assess the environmental effects of their proposed actions prior to making decisions. The range of actions covered by NEPA includes making decisions on permit applications, adopting federal land management actions, and constructing highways and other publicly-owned facilities.

nodes.title: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act
nodes.agency: Department of Health and Human Services
nodes.summary: Establishes national standards to protect sensitive patient health information from disclosure without consent.
nodes.text: HIPAA establishes national standards to protect individuals' medical records and other personal health information. The Privacy Rule requires appropriate safeguards to protect privacy and sets limits on uses and disclosures.

nodes.title: Clean Water Act
nodes.summary: Establishes the structure for regulating discharges of pollutants into U.S. waters and quality standards for surface waters.
nodes.text: The Clean Water Act establishes the basic structure for regulating discharges of pollutants into the waters of the United States and regulating quality standards for surface waters. The basis of the CWA was enacted in 1948 and was called the Federal Water Pollution Control Act, but the Act was significantly reorganized and expanded in 1972.

nodes.title: Endangered Species Act
nodes.summary: Provides for the conservation of species that are endangered or threatened and the ecosystems on which they depend.
nodes.text: The ESA provides a program for the conservation of threatened and endangered plants and animals and the habitats in which they are found. The law requires federal agencies to ensure that actions they authorize, fund, or carry out are not likely to jeopardize listed species.

nodes.title: Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act
nodes.summary: Known as Superfund, provides federal authority to respond to releases of hazardous substances.
nodes.text: CERCLA, commonly known as Superfund, was enacted by Congress to create a tax on the chemical and petroleum industries and provide broad Federal authority to respond directly to releases or threatened releases of hazardous substances that may endanger public health or the environment.

nodes.title: Federal Trade Commission Act
nodes.summary: Established the FTC and prohibits unfair methods of competition and unfair or deceptive acts or practices.
nodes.text: The Federal Trade Commission Act prohibits unfair methods of competition and unfair or deceptive acts or practices in or affecting commerce. The FTC enforces consumer protection laws and antitrust laws.

nodes.title: Securities Act of 1933
nodes.summary: Requires registration of securities offerings and disclosure of material information to investors.
nodes.text: The Securities Act of 1933 has two basic objectives: require that investors receive financial and other significant information concerning securities being offered for public sale; and prohibit deceit, misrepresentations, and other fraud in the sale of securities.

nodes.title: Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act
nodes.summary: Comprehensive financial regulatory reform enacted in response to the 2008 financial crisis.
nodes.text: The Dodd-Frank Act brought significant changes to financial regulation in the United States, including the creation of the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau and new oversight mechanisms for systemic risk in the financial system.

nodes.title: Civil Rights Act of 1964
nodes.summary: Landmark legislation prohibiting discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, or national origin.
nodes.text: The Civil Rights Act of 1964 outlaws discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, or national origin. Title VII specifically prohibits employment discrimination and created the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission.

nodes.title: Americans with Disabilities Act
nodes.summary: Prohibits discrimination against individuals with disabilities in employment, public accommodations, and government services.
nodes.text: The ADA prohibits discrimination against people with disabilities in several areas, including employment, transportation, public accommodations, communications, and access to state and local government programs and services.

nodes.title: Sherman Antitrust Act
nodes.summary: The first federal antitrust law, prohibiting monopolies and restraints of trade.
nodes.text: The Sherman Act outlaws every contract, combination, or conspiracy in restraint of trade, and any monopolization, attempted monopolization, or conspiracy or combination to monopolize.

nodes.title: Clayton Antitrust Act
nodes.summary: Strengthens antitrust regulation by prohibiting specific anticompetitive practices.
nodes.text: The Clayton Act addresses specific practices that the Sherman Act does not clearly prohibit, such as mergers and acquisitions that substantially lessen competition, exclusive dealing contracts, and interlocking directorates.

nodes.title: Fair Credit Reporting Act
nodes.summary: Regulates the collection, dissemination, and use of consumer credit information.
nodes.text: The FCRA promotes the accuracy, fairness, and privacy of consumer information contained in the files of consumer reporting agencies. It regulates the collection, dissemination, and use of consumer credit information.

nodes.title: Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act
nodes.summary: Requires financial institutions to explain information-sharing practices and protect sensitive data.
nodes.text: The GLBA requires financial institutions to explain their information-sharing practices to customers and to safeguard sensitive data. The Safeguards Rule requires companies to develop a written information security plan.

nodes.title: Sarbanes-Oxley Act
nodes.summary: Establishes enhanced financial disclosure requirements and corporate governance standards for public companies.
nodes.text: The Sarbanes-Oxley Act mandates strict reforms to improve financial disclosures from corporations and prevent accounting fraud. It created the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (PCAOB) to oversee auditing.

nodes.title: Resource Conservation and Recovery Act
nodes.summary: Governs the disposal of solid and hazardous waste, establishing cradle-to-grave tracking.
nodes.text: RCRA gives EPA the authority to control hazardous waste from cradle to grave. This includes the generation, transportation, treatment, storage, and disposal of hazardous waste.

nodes.title: Safe Drinking Water Act
nodes.summary: Protects public drinking water supplies by establishing standards and monitoring requirements.
nodes.text: The SDWA was established to protect the quality of drinking water in the U.S. It authorizes EPA to set national health-based standards for drinking water to protect against both naturally-occurring and man-made contaminants.

nodes.title: Federal Information Security Management Act
nodes.summary: Requires federal agencies to develop, document, and implement information security programs.
nodes.text: FISMA requires each federal agency to develop, document, and implement an agency-wide program to provide information security for the information and information systems that support the operations and assets of the agency.

nodes.title: E-Government Act of 2002
nodes.summary: Promotes use of electronic government services and requires privacy impact assessments.
nodes.text: The E-Government Act promotes the use of Internet-based information technology to make government information and services available to the public. It requires agencies to conduct privacy impact assessments before collecting personal information.

nodes.title: Paperwork Reduction Act
nodes.summary: Requires OMB approval before agencies collect information from the public.
nodes.text: The PRA requires federal agencies to obtain approval from OMB before collecting information from the public. It aims to minimize the paperwork burden and ensure that data collection has practical utility.

nodes.title: National Forest Management Act
nodes.summary: Governs the administration of national forests and requires land management planning.
nodes.text: NFMA is the primary statute governing the administration of national forests. It requires the Forest Service to develop land management plans for each unit of the National Forest System and establishes standards for timber sales.

nodes.title: Federal Land Policy and Management Act
nodes.summary: Establishes BLM's mandate and requires multiple-use management of public lands.
nodes.text: FLPMA establishes the policy that public lands be retained in federal ownership unless disposal serves the national interest. It requires the BLM to manage lands for multiple use and sustained yield.

nodes.title: National Historic Preservation Act
nodes.summary: Establishes the framework for historic preservation in the United States.
nodes.text: The NHPA established the National Register of Historic Places and requires federal agencies to take into account the effects of their undertakings on historic properties through the Section 106 review process.

nodes.title: Computer Fraud and Abuse Act
nodes.summary: Criminalizes unauthorized access to computers and computer networks.
nodes.text: The CFAA prohibits accessing a computer without authorization or exceeding authorized access. It covers federal computers, financial records, and computers used in interstate commerce.

nodes.title: Electronic Communications Privacy Act
nodes.summary: Extends wiretapping restrictions to electronic communications and stored data.
nodes.text: The ECPA extends government restrictions on wiretaps to include transmissions of electronic data by computer. It also prohibits access to stored electronic communications.

nodes.title: Children's Online Privacy Protection Act
nodes.summary: Imposes requirements on websites and online services directed at children under 13.
nodes.text: COPPA imposes certain requirements on operators of websites or online services directed to children under 13 years of age, and on operators that have actual knowledge that they are collecting personal information from a child under 13.

nodes.title: CAN-SPAM Act
nodes.summary: Establishes requirements for commercial email and gives recipients the right to opt out.
nodes.text: The CAN-SPAM Act sets the rules for commercial email, establishes requirements for commercial messages, gives recipients the right to have you stop emailing them, and spells out tough penalties for violations.

nodes.title: Securities Exchange Act of 1934
nodes.summary: Created the SEC and governs secondary trading of securities.
nodes.text: The Securities Exchange Act of 1934 created the Securities and Exchange Commission and gave it broad authority over all aspects of the securities industry, including the power to register, regulate, and oversee brokerage firms.

nodes.title: Investment Company Act of 1940
nodes.summary: Regulates the organization of investment companies and their activities.
nodes.text: The Investment Company Act regulates the organization of companies, including mutual funds, that engage primarily in investing, reinvesting, and trading in securities and whose own securities are offered to the investing public.

nodes.title: Investment Advisers Act of 1940
nodes.summary: Requires investment advisers to register with the SEC and establishes fiduciary duties.
nodes.text: The Investment Advisers Act regulates investment advisers. With certain exceptions, this Act requires that firms or sole practitioners compensated for advising others about securities investments must register with the SEC.

nodes.title: Bank Secrecy Act
nodes.summary: Requires financial institutions to assist government agencies in detecting and preventing money laundering.
nodes.text: The Bank Secrecy Act requires U.S. financial institutions to assist U.S. government agencies to detect and prevent money laundering. It requires keeping records of cash purchases and filing reports of cash transactions exceeding $10,000.

nodes.title: USA PATRIOT Act
nodes.summary: Expanded surveillance and investigation powers in response to terrorism threats.
nodes.text: The USA PATRIOT Act was enacted to deter and punish terrorist acts in the United States and around the world, to enhance law enforcement investigatory tools, and for other purposes. It significantly expanded surveillance authorities.

nodes.title: Telephone Consumer Protection Act
nodes.summary: Restricts telemarketing calls, autodialed calls, and text messages.
nodes.text: The TCPA restricts the making of telemarketing calls and the use of automatic telephone dialing systems and prerecorded voice messages. It also restricts the use of SMS text messages and fax machines.

nodes.title: Communications Act of 1934
nodes.summary: Created the FCC and established the framework for regulating communications.
nodes.text: The Communications Act of 1934 established the Federal Communications Commission and gave it authority to regulate interstate and foreign commerce in communication by wire and radio.

nodes.title: Telecommunications Act of 1996
nodes.summary: Major overhaul of telecommunications law promoting competition in local telephone markets.
nodes.text: The Telecommunications Act of 1996 was the first major overhaul of telecommunications law in almost 62 years. Its main purpose was to promote competition in local telephone markets.

nodes.title: Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act
nodes.summary: Authorizes FDA to oversee the safety of food, drugs, medical devices, and cosmetics.
nodes.text: The FDCA is the basic food and drug law of the United States. It gives authority to the FDA to oversee the safety of food, drugs, medical devices, and cosmetics.

nodes.title: Occupational Safety and Health Act
nodes.summary: Ensures workplace safety and health through standards and enforcement.
nodes.text: The OSH Act was passed to prevent workers from being killed or seriously harmed at work. The law requires employers to provide their employees with working conditions that are free of known dangers.

nodes.title: Employee Retirement Income Security Act
nodes.summary: Sets standards for pension and health plans to protect employee benefits.
nodes.text: ERISA is a federal law that sets minimum standards for most voluntarily established retirement and health plans in private industry to provide protection for individuals in these plans.

nodes.title: Fair Labor Standards Act
nodes.summary: Establishes minimum wage, overtime pay, and child labor standards.
nodes.text: The FLSA establishes minimum wage, overtime pay, recordkeeping, and youth employment standards affecting employees in the private sector and in Federal, State, and local governments.

nodes.title: National Labor Relations Act
nodes.summary: Protects employees' rights to organize and engage in collective bargaining.
nodes.text: The NLRA extends rights to many private sector employees, including the right to organize and bargain collectively with their employers, and to engage in other protected concerted activity.

nodes.title: Family and Medical Leave Act
nodes.summary: Provides eligible employees with unpaid, job-protected leave for family and medical reasons.
nodes.text: The FMLA entitles eligible employees of covered employers to take unpaid, job-protected leave for specified family and medical reasons with continuation of group health insurance coverage.

nodes.title: Age Discrimination in Employment Act
nodes.summary: Prohibits employment discrimination against individuals 40 years of age or older.
nodes.text: The ADEA forbids age discrimination against people who are age 40 or older in hiring, promotion, discharge, compensation, or terms, conditions or privileges of employment.

nodes.title: Title IX of the Education Amendments
nodes.summary: Prohibits sex-based discrimination in education programs receiving federal funding.
nodes.text: Title IX prohibits discrimination on the basis of sex in any federally funded education program or activity. It applies to all aspects of education programs, including athletics.

nodes.title: Rehabilitation Act of 1973
nodes.summary: Prohibits discrimination against individuals with disabilities in federal programs.
nodes.text: The Rehabilitation Act prohibits discrimination on the basis of disability in programs conducted by federal agencies, in programs receiving federal financial assistance, and in federal employment.

nodes.title: FERPA Regulations
nodes.summary: Implements FERPA requirements for educational agencies and institutions receiving federal funds.
nodes.text: These regulations implement the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA), which affords parents the right to have access to their children's education records, the right to seek to have the records amended, and the right to have some control over the disclosure of personally identifiable information from the education records.

nodes.title: DOJ FOIA Regulations
nodes.summary: Department of Justice procedures for processing FOIA requests and administrative appeals.
nodes.text: These regulations set forth the procedures the Department of Justice follows in processing requests for records under the Freedom of Information Act. They describe how to make a request, how fees are assessed, and how to file an administrative appeal.

nodes.title: National Ambient Air Quality Standards
nodes.summary: Establishes air quality standards for six criteria pollutants to protect public health and welfare.
nodes.text: The national primary ambient air quality standards define levels of air quality which the Administrator judges are necessary, with an adequate margin of safety, to protect the public health. The national secondary ambient air quality standards define levels necessary to protect the public welfare from any known or anticipated adverse effects of a pollutant.

nodes.title: CEQ NEPA Regulations
nodes.summary: Implements NEPA requirements for environmental impact statements and environmental assessments.
nodes.text: These regulations implement the procedural provisions of the National Environmental Policy Act. They establish the basic framework for environmental impact statements, environmental assessments, categorical exclusions, and other NEPA procedures.

nodes.title: ACUS Rulemaking Recommendations
nodes.agency: Administrative Conference of the United States
nodes.summary: Best practices and recommendations for federal agency rulemaking procedures.
nodes.text: The Administrative Conference issues recommendations to improve the efficiency, adequacy, and fairness of agency procedures. These recommendations address notice-and-comment rulemaking, retrospective review of regulations, and public participation in the regulatory process.

nodes.title: HIPAA Privacy Rule
nodes.agency: Department of Health and Human Services
nodes.summary: Establishes national standards for protection of individually identifiable health information.
nodes.text: The HIPAA Privacy Rule establishes national standards to protect individuals' medical records and other personal health information and applies to health plans, health care clearinghouses, and those health care providers that conduct certain health care transactions electronically.

nodes.title: HIPAA Security Rule
nodes.agency: Department of Health and Human Services
nodes.summary: Establishes standards for safeguarding electronic protected health information.
nodes.text: The Security Rule requires appropriate administrative, physical and technical safeguards to ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and security of electronic protected health information.

nodes.title: SEC Rule 10b-5
nodes.summary: Prohibits fraud in connection with the purchase or sale of securities.
nodes.text: It shall be unlawful for any person to employ any device, scheme, or artifice to defraud, or to make any untrue statement of a material fact or to omit to state a material fact necessary in order to make the statements made not misleading.

nodes.title: Waters of the United States Rule
nodes.summary: Defines which waters are protected under the Clean Water Act.
nodes.text: This rule defines the scope of waters federally regulated under the Clean Water Act. The definition includes traditional navigable waters, territorial seas, interstate waters, and other waters that significantly affect those waters.

nodes.title: NPDES Permit Regulations
nodes.summary: Governs permits for point source discharges under the Clean Water Act.
nodes.text: The NPDES permit program controls water pollution by regulating point sources that discharge pollutants into waters of the United States. These regulations establish the procedures for applying for and obtaining permits.

nodes.title: RCRA Hazardous Waste Regulations
nodes.summary: Establishes requirements for management of hazardous waste from generation to disposal.
nodes.text: These regulations establish the hazardous waste management system, including identification and listing of hazardous wastes, standards for generators, transporters, and treatment, storage, and disposal facilities.

nodes.title: National Oil and Hazardous Substances Pollution Contingency Plan
nodes.summary: Establishes procedures for responding to releases of hazardous substances.
nodes.text: The NCP, also known as the Superfund cleanup regulations, provides the organizational structure and procedures for preparing for and responding to discharges of oil and releases of hazardous substances.

nodes.title: NIST SP 800-53 Security Controls
nodes.agency: National Institute of Standards and Technology
nodes.summary: Catalog of security and privacy controls for federal information systems.
nodes.text: This publication provides a catalog of security and privacy controls for federal information systems and organizations to protect organizational operations, assets, individuals, and the Nation from a diverse set of threats and risks.

nodes.title: OMB Circular A-130
nodes.summary: Establishes policies for managing federal information resources.
nodes.text: This Circular establishes general policy for the planning, budgeting, governance, acquisition, and management of Federal information, personnel, equipment, funds, IT resources, and supporting infrastructure and services.

nodes.title: FedRAMP Authorization Requirements
nodes.summary: Security requirements for cloud services used by federal agencies.
nodes.text: FedRAMP provides a standardized approach to security assessment, authorization, and continuous monitoring for cloud products and services used by the federal government.

nodes.title: FTC Safeguards Rule
nodes.summary: Information security requirements for financial institutions under GLBA.
nodes.text: The Safeguards Rule requires financial institutions to develop, implement, and maintain a comprehensive information security program. Recent amendments strengthened requirements for access controls, encryption, and incident response.

nodes.title: ADA Title II Regulations
nodes.summary: Implements ADA requirements for state and local government services.
nodes.text: These regulations implement Title II of the ADA, which prohibits discrimination on the basis of disability by state and local government entities. Recent updates address web accessibility requirements.

nodes.title: ADA Title III Regulations
nodes.summary: Implements ADA requirements for public accommodations.
nodes.text: These regulations implement Title III of the ADA, which prohibits discrimination on the basis of disability in places of public accommodation and commercial facilities.

nodes.title: Title IX Regulations
nodes.summary: Implements Title IX's prohibition on sex discrimination in education.
nodes.text: These regulations implement Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972, addressing sexual harassment, athletics, and discrimination on the basis of sex in education programs receiving federal funding.

nodes.title: COPPA Rule
nodes.summary: Implements requirements for collecting personal information from children online.
nodes.text: The COPPA Rule details what operators of websites and online services directed to children under 13 must do to protect children's privacy and safety online, including requirements for verifiable parental consent.

nodes.title: OSHA Safety Standards
nodes.summary: General industry occupational safety and health standards.
nodes.text: These regulations establish occupational safety and health standards for general industry workplaces, covering areas such as hazard communication, personal protective equipment, machine guarding, and electrical safety.

nodes.title: FLSA Overtime Regulations
nodes.summary: Defines exemptions from minimum wage and overtime requirements.
nodes.text: These regulations define the executive, administrative, professional, outside sales, and computer employee exemptions from the FLSA's minimum wage and overtime requirements.

nodes.title: ERISA Fiduciary Rule
nodes.summary: Defines fiduciary duties for retirement plan investment advice.
nodes.text: These regulations define when investment advice providers become fiduciaries under ERISA and establish standards of conduct for fiduciary investment advice to retirement plan participants.

nodes.title: SEC Regulation D
nodes.summary: Provides exemptions from securities registration for private placements.
nodes.text: Regulation D provides exemptions from the registration requirements of the Securities Act of 1933 for certain offerings. Rules 504, 506(b), and 506(c) establish the conditions for exempt private placements.

nodes.title: SEC Regulation S-K
nodes.summary: Prescribes disclosure requirements for SEC filings.
nodes.text: Regulation S-K sets forth disclosure requirements for various SEC filings used by public companies. It covers items such as business descriptions, risk factors, management discussion and analysis, and executive compensation.

nodes.title: FCC Open Internet Rules
nodes.summary: Establishes net neutrality rules for broadband internet access services.
nodes.text: These rules prohibit broadband internet access service providers from blocking, throttling, or engaging in paid prioritization of lawful content, applications, services, or non-harmful devices.

nodes.title: FDA New Drug Application Regulations
nodes.summary: Governs the approval process for new drugs.
nodes.text: These regulations describe the procedures for filing and reviewing new drug applications (NDAs) and abbreviated new drug applications (ANDAs). They establish requirements for demonstrating safety and efficacy.

nodes.title: Chevron U.S.A., Inc. v. Natural Resources Defense Council
nodes.summary: Established the Chevron deference doctrine requiring courts to defer to reasonable agency interpretations of ambiguous statutes.
nodes.text: When a court reviews an agency's construction of the statute which it administers, the court must first determine whether Congress has directly spoken to the precise question at issue. If the statute is silent or ambiguous, the question is whether the agency's answer is based on a permissible construction of the statute.

nodes.title: Auer v. Robbins
nodes.summary: Established Auer deference to agency interpretations of their own ambiguous regulations.
nodes.text: An agency's interpretation of its own regulation is controlling unless plainly erroneous or inconsistent with the regulation. This deference is warranted because the agency is the author of the regulation and is in a better position to reconstruct its original intent.

nodes.title: Motor Vehicle Manufacturers Ass'n v. State Farm
nodes.summary: Established the arbitrary and capricious standard for judicial review of agency rulemaking.
nodes.text: The scope of review under the arbitrary and capricious standard is narrow and a court is not to substitute its judgment for that of the agency. Nevertheless, the agency must examine the relevant data and articulate a satisfactory explanation for its action.

nodes.title: Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimondo
nodes.summary: Overruled Chevron deference, holding that courts must exercise independent judgment in interpreting statutes.
nodes.text: Chevron is overruled. Courts must exercise their independent judgment in deciding whether an agency has acted within its statutory authority. The APA requires courts to decide all relevant questions of law and interpret statutory provisions.

nodes.title: Marbury v. Madison
nodes.summary: Established the principle of judicial review, giving courts power to declare laws unconstitutional.
nodes.text: It is emphatically the province and duty of the judicial department to say what the law is. Those who apply the rule to particular cases, must of necessity expound and interpret that rule. If two laws conflict with each other, the courts must decide on the operation of each.

nodes.title: West Virginia v. EPA
nodes.summary: Applied the major questions doctrine, requiring clear congressional authorization for agency rules of vast economic and political significance.
nodes.text: In certain extraordinary cases, both separation of powers principles and a practical understanding of legislative intent make us reluctant to read into ambiguous statutory text the delegation claimed to be lurking there. We expect Congress to speak clearly when authorizing an agency to exercise powers of vast economic and political significance.

nodes.title: Kisor v. Wilkie
nodes.summary: Limited but preserved Auer deference, requiring genuine ambiguity and reasonable interpretation.
nodes.text: A court should not afford Auer deference unless the regulation is genuinely ambiguous. And when we use that term, we mean it—genuinely ambiguous, even after a court has resorted to all the standard tools of interpretation.

nodes.title: Sackett v. EPA
nodes.summary: Narrowed the scope of waters protected under the Clean Water Act.
nodes.text: The CWA's use of 'waters' encompasses only those relatively permanent, standing or continuously flowing bodies of water forming geographic features that are described in ordinary parlance as streams, oceans, rivers, and lakes.

nodes.title: Biden v. Nebraska
nodes.summary: Struck down student loan forgiveness program, applying major questions doctrine.
nodes.text: The Secretary's plan has modified the existing loan forgiveness legislation so completely that it effectively created a new legislative scheme. The question is whether Congress gave the Secretary such authority, and we conclude it did not.

nodes.title: SEC v. Jarkesy
nodes.summary: Held that SEC administrative enforcement proceedings seeking civil penalties violate Seventh Amendment jury trial right.
nodes.text: When the SEC seeks civil penalties against a defendant for securities fraud, the Seventh Amendment entitles the defendant to a jury trial. The Seventh Amendment preserves the right to a jury trial in suits at common law.

nodes.title: Corner Post v. Board of Governors
nodes.summary: Held that APA statute of limitations begins when plaintiff is injured, not when regulation is issued.
nodes.text: An APA claim does not accrue until the plaintiff has been injured by final agency action. The six-year statute of limitations runs from that injury, not from the date the regulation was promulgated.

nodes.title: Citizens United v. FEC
nodes.summary: Held that corporate independent political expenditures are protected speech under the First Amendment.
nodes.text: The First Amendment prohibits the government from restricting independent political expenditures by corporations, associations, and labor unions. Political speech does not lose constitutional protection simply because its source is a corporation.

nodes.title: Griswold v. Connecticut
nodes.summary: Recognized a constitutional right to privacy in matters of contraception and marital relations.
nodes.text: The specific guarantees in the Bill of Rights have penumbras, formed by emanations from those guarantees that help give them life and substance. Various constitutional guarantees create zones of privacy.

nodes.title: Brown v. Board of Education
nodes.summary: Declared racial segregation in public schools unconstitutional.
nodes.text: Separate educational facilities are inherently unequal. Segregation of children in public schools solely on the basis of race deprives children of the minority group of equal educational opportunities.

nodes.title: Miranda v. Arizona
nodes.summary: Required police to inform suspects of their rights before custodial interrogation.
nodes.text: The prosecution may not use statements stemming from custodial interrogation of the defendant unless it demonstrates the use of procedural safeguards effective to secure the privilege against self-incrimination.

nodes.title: McCulloch v. Maryland
nodes.summary: Established Congress's implied powers and federal supremacy over state laws.
nodes.text: Let the end be legitimate, let it be within the scope of the constitution, and all means which are appropriate, which are plainly adapted to that end, which are not prohibited, but consist with the letter and spirit of the constitution, are constitutional.

nodes.title: Gibbons v. Ogden
nodes.summary: Broadly interpreted Congress's Commerce Clause power over interstate commerce.
nodes.text: Commerce among the States cannot stop at the external boundary line of each State, but may be introduced into the interior. The power of Congress to regulate commerce is complete in itself.

nodes.title: Wickard v. Filburn
nodes.summary: Expanded Commerce Clause power to activities with substantial aggregate effects on interstate commerce.
nodes.text: Even if an activity be local and though it may not be regarded as commerce, it may still be reached by Congress if it exerts a substantial economic effect on interstate commerce.

nodes.title: United States v. Lopez
nodes.summary: Limited Commerce Clause power, requiring substantial effect on interstate commerce.
nodes.text: The Commerce Clause power has three categories: channels of interstate commerce, instrumentalities of interstate commerce, and activities that substantially affect interstate commerce.

nodes.title: Youngstown Sheet & Tube Co. v. Sawyer
nodes.summary: Established the framework for analyzing presidential power and executive action.
nodes.text: Presidential powers are not fixed but fluctuate depending upon their disjunction or conjunction with those of Congress. When the President acts pursuant to congressional authorization, his power is at its maximum.

nodes.title: NFIB v. Sebelius
nodes.summary: Upheld the Affordable Care Act's individual mandate as a valid exercise of taxing power.
nodes.text: The individual mandate is not a valid exercise of Congress's Commerce Clause power, but it is a valid exercise of Congress's taxing power. The mandate can be construed as a tax on those who do not have health insurance.

nodes.title: Obergefell v. Hodges
nodes.summary: Held that same-sex couples have a constitutional right to marry.
nodes.text: The right to marry is a fundamental right inherent in the liberty of the person, and under the Due Process and Equal Protection Clauses of the Fourteenth Amendment, couples of the same sex may not be deprived of that right.

nodes.title: Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization
nodes.summary: Overruled Roe v. Wade and held there is no constitutional right to abortion.
nodes.text: The Constitution does not confer a right to abortion; Roe and Casey are overruled; and the authority to regulate abortion is returned to the people and their elected representatives.

nodes.title: Murphy v. NCAA
nodes.summary: Struck down federal law prohibiting states from authorizing sports betting under anti-commandeering doctrine.
nodes.text: The anti-commandeering doctrine prohibits Congress from issuing orders directly to state legislatures. Congress cannot compel states to enact or refrain from enacting any particular legislation.

nodes.title: Ashcroft v. Free Speech Coalition
nodes.summary: Struck down provisions of CPPA criminalizing virtual child pornography as overbroad.
nodes.text: The CPPA prohibits speech that records no crime and creates no victims by its production. Virtual child pornography is not intrinsically related to the sexual abuse of children.

nodes.title: Massachusetts v. EPA
nodes.summary: Held that EPA has authority to regulate greenhouse gas emissions under the Clean Air Act.
nodes.text: Because greenhouse gases fit well within the Clean Air Act's capacious definition of 'air pollutant,' EPA has statutory authority to regulate emission of such gases from new motor vehicles.

nodes.title: Free Enterprise Fund v. PCAOB
nodes.summary: Struck down PCAOB's dual for-cause removal protection as violating separation of powers.
nodes.text: The dual for-cause limitations on the removal of Board members contravene the Constitution's separation of powers. The President cannot take care that the laws be faithfully executed if he cannot oversee the faithfulness of the officers who execute them.

nodes.title: Executive Order 12866 - Regulatory Planning and Review
nodes.summary: Establishes principles for regulatory planning and review, including cost-benefit analysis requirements.
nodes.text: Federal agencies should promulgate only such regulations as are required by law, are necessary to interpret the law, or are made necessary by compelling public need. In deciding whether and how to regulate, agencies should assess all costs and benefits of available regulatory alternatives.

nodes.title: Executive Order 13563 - Improving Regulation and Regulatory Review
nodes.summary: Supplements E.O. 12866 with principles for retrospective review and public participation.
nodes.text: Our regulatory system must protect public health, welfare, safety, and our environment while promoting economic growth, innovation, competitiveness, and job creation. Regulations must be based on the best available science.

nodes.title: Executive Order 14094 - Modernizing Regulatory Review
nodes.summary: Updates regulatory review process to advance public welfare and address modern challenges.
nodes.text: This order modernizes the regulatory review process to ensure it is equipped to deliver regulations that advance the public interest. It emphasizes distributional consequences and equity considerations in regulatory analysis.

nodes.title: Executive Order 14110 - Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy AI
nodes.summary: Establishes requirements for AI safety, security, and trustworthiness across federal government.
nodes.text: This order establishes new standards for AI safety and security, protects Americans' privacy, advances equity and civil rights, stands up for consumers and workers, promotes innovation and competition, and advances American leadership around the world.

nodes.title: Executive Order 13988 - Preventing and Combating Discrimination
nodes.summary: Extends protections against discrimination on the basis of gender identity or sexual orientation.
nodes.text: Every person should be treated with respect and dignity and should be able to live without fear, no matter who they are or whom they love. Children should be able to learn without worrying about whether they will be denied access to the restroom, the locker room, or school sports.

nodes.title: Executive Order 14008 - Tackling the Climate Crisis
nodes.summary: Establishes climate change as an essential element of foreign policy and national security.
nodes.text: The United States will exercise its leadership to promote a significant increase in global ambition. It is the policy of my Administration to organize and deploy the full capacity of its agencies to combat the climate crisis.

nodes.title: Executive Order 13985 - Advancing Racial Equity
nodes.summary: Directs agencies to advance equity and support underserved communities.
nodes.text: It is the policy of my Administration that the Federal Government should pursue a comprehensive approach to advancing equity for all, including people of color and others who have been historically underserved, marginalized, and adversely affected by persistent poverty and inequality.

nodes.title: Executive Order 14028 - Improving the Nation's Cybersecurity
nodes.summary: Modernizes federal cybersecurity standards and improves software supply chain security.
nodes.text: The Federal Government must improve its efforts to identify, deter, protect against, detect, and respond to persistent and increasingly sophisticated malicious cyber campaigns. The government must lead by example and modernize its approach to cybersecurity.

nodes.title: Executive Order 14117 - Protecting Americans' Sensitive Data
nodes.summary: Restricts access to Americans' bulk sensitive personal data by countries of concern.
nodes.text: This order addresses the national security threat posed by the continued effort of certain countries of concern to access Americans' bulk sensitive personal data and certain United States Government-related data.

nodes.title: Executive Order 14081 - Advancing Biotechnology and Biomanufacturing
nodes.summary: Advances biotechnology and biomanufacturing innovation for economic and national security.
nodes.text: It is the policy of my Administration to coordinate a whole-of-government approach to advance biotechnology and biomanufacturing towards innovative solutions in health, climate change, energy, food security, agriculture, supply chain resilience, and national and economic security.

nodes.title: Executive Order 14058 - Customer Experience and Service Delivery
nodes.summary: Directs agencies to transform federal customer experience and service delivery.
nodes.text: The Government must recommit to being of the people, by the people, and for the people. Government must be held accountable for designing and delivering services with a focus on the actual experience of the people whom it is meant to serve.

nodes.title: Environmental Protection Agency
nodes.summary: Independent agency responsible for protecting human health and the environment.
nodes.text: The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is an independent executive agency of the United States federal government tasked with environmental protection matters. The EPA regulates air and water quality, pesticides, and hazardous waste.

nodes.title: Department of Education
nodes.summary: Cabinet-level department responsible for federal education policy and programs.
nodes.text: The Department of Education is a Cabinet-level department of the United States government. It administers federal assistance to education and enforces federal educational laws regarding privacy and civil rights.

nodes.title: Department of Justice
nodes.summary: Cabinet-level department responsible for enforcement of federal laws.
nodes.text: The Department of Justice (DOJ) is a cabinet-level department responsible for the enforcement of the law and administration of justice in the United States.

nodes.title: Department of Health and Human Services
nodes.summary: Cabinet-level department responsible for protecting the health of Americans.
nodes.text: The Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) is the United States government's principal agency for protecting the health of all Americans and providing essential human services.

nodes.title: Securities and Exchange Commission
nodes.summary: Independent agency responsible for enforcing federal securities laws and regulating the securities industry.
nodes.text: The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is an independent agency of the United States federal government, created in the aftermath of the Wall Street Crash of 1929. The primary purpose of the SEC is to enforce the law against market manipulation.

nodes.title: Federal Trade Commission
nodes.summary: Independent agency focused on consumer protection and preventing anticompetitive business practices.
nodes.text: The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) is an independent agency of the United States government whose principal mission is the enforcement of civil U.S. antitrust law and the promotion of consumer protection.

nodes.title: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service
nodes.summary: Agency responsible for managing fish, wildlife, and natural habitats.
nodes.text: The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service is a bureau within the Department of the Interior dedicated to the management of fish, wildlife, and natural habitats. The agency implements the Endangered Species Act.

nodes.title: Office of Management and Budget
nodes.summary: Executive Office of the President component overseeing federal agency budgets and regulations.
nodes.text: The Office of Management and Budget is the largest office within the Executive Office of the President. OMB's predominant mission is to assist the President in overseeing the preparation of the federal budget and to supervise its administration in Executive Branch agencies.

nodes.title: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau
nodes.summary: Agency responsible for consumer protection in the financial sector.
nodes.text: The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) is an agency of the United States government responsible for consumer protection in the financial sector. The CFPB was created by the Dodd-Frank Act.

nodes.title: Federal Communications Commission
nodes.summary: Independent agency regulating interstate and international communications.
nodes.text: The Federal Communications Commission regulates interstate and international communications by radio, television, wire, satellite, and cable. The FCC maintains jurisdiction over broadband access, spectrum management, and media regulation.

nodes.title: Food and Drug Administration
nodes.summary: Agency responsible for protecting public health through regulation of food, drugs, and medical devices.
nodes.text: The Food and Drug Administration is responsible for protecting the public health by ensuring the safety, efficacy, and security of human and veterinary drugs, biological products, and medical devices.

nodes.title: Occupational Safety and Health Administration
nodes.summary: Agency responsible for ensuring safe and healthful working conditions.
nodes.text: The Occupational Safety and Health Administration is an agency of the United States Department of Labor. OSHA's mission is to ensure safe and healthful working conditions by setting and enforcing standards and by providing training, outreach, education, and assistance.

nodes.title: Department of Labor
nodes.summary: Cabinet department responsible for occupational safety, wage and hour standards, and employment services.
nodes.text: The Department of Labor is a cabinet-level department of the U.S. federal government responsible for occupational safety, wage and hour standards, unemployment insurance benefits, reemployment services, and some economic statistics.

nodes.title: Equal Employment Opportunity Commission
nodes.summary: Agency responsible for enforcing federal laws prohibiting employment discrimination.
nodes.text: The Equal Employment Opportunity Commission is the federal agency that enforces civil rights laws against workplace discrimination. The EEOC investigates discrimination complaints based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, or genetic information.

nodes.title: National Labor Relations Board
nodes.summary: Agency responsible for enforcing labor law in relation to collective bargaining and unfair labor practices.
nodes.text: The National Labor Relations Board is an independent agency of the federal government that enforces labor law in relation to collective bargaining and unfair labor practices. It conducts elections for labor union representation.

nodes.title: National Institute of Standards and Technology
nodes.summary: Agency responsible for developing technology, metrics, and standards.
nodes.text: The National Institute of Standards and Technology is a physical sciences laboratory and non-regulatory agency of the United States Department of Commerce. NIST develops cybersecurity frameworks and standards.

nodes.title: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency
nodes.summary: Agency responsible for protecting the nation's critical infrastructure from cyber and physical threats.
nodes.text: CISA is the nation's risk advisor, working with partners to defend against today's threats and collaborating to build more secure and resilient infrastructure for the future.

nodes.title: Department of the Treasury
nodes.summary: Cabinet department responsible for economic and financial policy.
nodes.text: The Department of the Treasury is responsible for promoting economic prosperity and ensuring the financial security of the United States. It manages federal finances, collects taxes, and produces currency.

nodes.title: Financial Crimes Enforcement Network
nodes.summary: Agency responsible for safeguarding the financial system from illicit use.
nodes.text: FinCEN is a bureau of the U.S. Department of the Treasury that collects and analyzes information about financial transactions to combat domestic and international money laundering, terrorist financing, and other financial crimes.

nodes.title: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission
nodes.summary: Independent agency regulating the interstate transmission of electricity, natural gas, and oil.
nodes.text: FERC is an independent agency that regulates the interstate transmission of electricity, natural gas, and oil. FERC also reviews proposals to build liquefied natural gas terminals and interstate natural gas pipelines.

nodes.title: Department of Agriculture
nodes.summary: Cabinet department responsible for developing and executing federal laws related to farming, agriculture, forestry, and food.
nodes.text: The United States Department of Agriculture is responsible for developing and executing federal government policy on farming, agriculture, forestry, rural economic development, and food.

nodes.title: U.S. Forest Service
nodes.summary: Agency responsible for managing national forests and grasslands.
nodes.text: The U.S. Forest Service is an agency of the U.S. Department of Agriculture that administers the nation's 154 national forests and 20 national grasslands. It manages these lands for multiple uses including timber, recreation, and wildlife.

nodes.title: Bureau of Land Management
nodes.summary: Agency responsible for managing federal public lands.
nodes.text: The Bureau of Land Management is an agency within the United States Department of the Interior that administers more than 245 million acres of public lands. BLM manages these lands for multiple use and sustained yield.

nodes.title: National Park Service
nodes.summary: Agency responsible for managing national parks and monuments.
nodes.text: The National Park Service is an agency of the United States federal government within the Department of the Interior that manages all national parks, many national monuments, and other conservation and historical properties.

nodes.title: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers
nodes.summary: Agency responsible for water resources development, flood control, and wetlands permits.
nodes.text: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers is a federal agency that designs and builds public works infrastructure and provides engineering services for military and civilian purposes. It issues Section 404 permits for wetlands under the Clean Water Act.

nodes.title: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration
nodes.summary: Agency responsible for monitoring and predicting changes in climate, weather, oceans, and coasts.
nodes.text: NOAA is an agency that enriches life through science. It monitors daily weather, provides severe weather warnings, charts seas, guides management of marine resources, and studies ecosystems.

nodes.title: Council on Environmental Quality
nodes.summary: White House office responsible for coordinating federal environmental efforts.
nodes.text: The Council on Environmental Quality coordinates federal environmental efforts and works closely with agencies and other White House offices in the development of environmental and energy policies.

nodes.title: Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs
nodes.summary: OMB office responsible for reviewing draft regulations and coordinating federal information policy.
nodes.text: OIRA is the United States federal government regulatory body. It reviews collections of information under the Paperwork Reduction Act, reviews draft regulations under Executive Order 12866, and develops and oversees the implementation of government-wide policies.

nodes.title: General Services Administration
nodes.summary: Agency responsible for managing government property and providing workplaces and acquisition services.
nodes.text: The General Services Administration is an independent agency of the United States government established to help manage and support the basic functioning of federal agencies. GSA manages FedRAMP for cloud security authorization.
